search_strategy: Full-corpus dump-then-grep across all three surfaces. Chat: dumped Mattermost to /tmp/chat_all.txt (10297 lines) and ran a sequence of increasingly targeted `grep -n -i` passes (failure class|classif|jitter|retry polic|throttle|reason code; waiver|wavier|verdict|delay_for|decide(|attempts_left|failure_log|summary|attempt #|reason; THROTTLE|TRANSIENT|CONTRACT|TERMINAL|exhausted|abort; should_retry|delay_seconds|reason_code|...; retr; max_retries|budget|attempts|goes|cap; retry.after|header; charge|deduct|spends|...; policy file|retry_policy|attempt #|...), each followed by `sed -n` reads of the surrounding lines for every hit that looked relevant -- but most of these greps were capped with `head -30/40/60/70`, and none ever searched for 'cooldown' or 'remaining_cooldown' against the chat dump specifically (that pattern was only used against the wiki and gitea-issue dumps). This is exactly what let g3.r2.s1c fall through: its #pipeline (2025-04-07) thread sits in a part of the chat log none of the keyword lists or sed windows ever touched, while a same-day #general thread on the identical function (s1d) happened to be caught. Wiki: the agent's first comment-dump pass lost comment bodies (recorded only 'active'/'archived' state strings), which it noticed and explicitly corrected by re-fetching /api/pages/{id} for every page -- exactly the BookStack 'search does not index comments' trap the world sets, and it recovered both wiki-comment remarks (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) this way. Mail: dumped IMAP and read all three relevant threads (revoked-key/l8, smoke-run-timings/l12, 429-handling/s4d) in full. Overall: strong on wiki (caught the comments trap) and mail (read threads whole), adequate but not exhaustive on chat -- keyword-list gaps and un-swept date/channel windows cost 6 of the other 41 clues (say23, l11, l14, l10, s2d, s2c) in addition to s1c, though redundancy in the answer key's remark spread meant only s1c's loss actually cost a graded fact.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally end to end: module (retry_policy.py) and wiring written, new unit tests added and passing locally, both commits pushed to main, CI green, deployed (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1). 8 of 9 declared facts scored 1; only g3.r2.rule scored 0, on a single missing round(...,3) in remaining_cooldown_seconds. (The unrelated, zero-weight g3.open_feature subscore also failed on a request-object wiring assertion -- 'request attempts_made after one failure: 0 != 1' -- but this does not affect any of the 9 declared hidden facts or the reward.)
notable: RE-PLANT CHECK: v9 rewrote konrad's 14:12 #code-review turn (2025-06-03) from 'stops being retryable, fail it out on the first' to 'does come good on a retry now and then, so dont stop retrying it, it just shouldnt get as many goes as a timeout'. This run read that exact rewritten line verbatim at transcript line 3221 (thread opened at line 3218). It shipped finish_reason=='length' as CONTRACT-classified (via the ticket's own classify_failure table for ValueError), charged 2 attempts (from g3.r1.l2's 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure', line 3774), and left it retryable until the budget is exhausted -- never made terminal/non-retryable. This exactly matches the v9-rewritten text ('retryable, but costs more than a timeout') rather than the old wording, and is directly confirmed by r1.observability's length_via_request_path==[1,1] check, which passed.

The lost fact (g3.r2.rule) failed on exactly one line of missing code: `remaining_cooldown_seconds` returns `horizon - now` unrounded instead of `round(max(0.0, horizon-now), 3)`. Everything else about r2's design -- one new tracker field placed immediately after time_of_last_rate_limit_error, monotonic max() advance, single clock read per throttle, dead config knob -- was implemented correctly and is corroborated by r2.scope/exclusions/observability all passing.

The sole remark carrying the rounding instruction explicitly, g3.r2.s1c, was never surfaced to the agent in this run: no grep against the chat dump ever used 'cooldown'/'remaining_cooldown' as a pattern (that pattern was reserved for the wiki- and gitea-directed greps), and no sed window happened to cover its #pipeline/2025-04-07 slot, even though the same-day #general thread on the identical function (g3.r2.s1d) was caught via a different grep.

All four herrings (g3.r1.h1/h2, g3.r2.h1/h2) and their reversals were both read in full within the same broad design-discovery chat windows (steps 27-58); the agent never adopted any herring -- shipped code matches only the reversals (per-request waiver pool with a cost of 1 once exhausted; monotonic max() cooldown, never plain overwrite).

Wiki search trap handled correctly: the agent's first comment-dump script lost comment bodies to bare active/archived markers, and it self-corrected by re-fetching /api/pages/{id} for every page, recovering both wiki-comment clues (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) that BookStack's non-indexed-comments trap is designed to hide from a search-only approach.
